title: Women

vibeProfile.oneLine: A semi-famous poet lurches through affairs, readings and hangovers.

summary: Now a semi-famous poet, Henry Chinaski lurches through a string of affairs, readings and hangovers in a bruising, self-lacerating comedy about desire and its wreckage. Bukowski's novel is blunt, often crude and unsparing about its narrator's failings, chronicling middle-aged appetite with the same flat, funny directness as his other Chinaski books. Not for every reader, but for admirers it is Bukowski doing exactly what he did best: turning a messy life into deadpan literature.
whyReadIt: Late-Chinaski Bukowski on desire and its wreckage, crude and unsparing. Blunt, funny, and definitely not for everyone.

funFacts.text: Like most of Bukowski's fiction, it is closely, unflatteringly autobiographical.
